card.line: Syria, called Aram in the Old Testament, was the land north of Israel, home to Damascus and to kings who fought Israel and Judah.

moments.title: Naaman the commander
moments.text: Naaman, the commander of the king of Aram's army, was a great man, but he had leprosy. A young girl taken from Israel told his wife about the prophet in Samaria, and the king sent Naaman to Israel with a letter and gifts.

moments.title: Aram's king plans war
moments.text: The king of Aram was at war against Israel and told his servants where his camp would be. Elisha kept warning Israel's king, so the angry king of Aram demanded to know who was on Israel's side.

moments.title: Elisha and Hazael in Damascus
moments.text: Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad, king of Aram, was sick. Hazael brought a gift and asked if the king would recover, and Elisha said the LORD had shown him that Hazael would be king over Aram.

moments.title: Aram's head is Damascus
moments.text: Aram joined with Ephraim in a plot against Judah, and Ahaz and his people trembled. The LORD told Isaiah to say that the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin.

moments.title: Jesus' fame spreads
moments.text: News about Jesus spread all over Syria. People brought Him all who were ill, in pain, demon-possessed, having seizures, or paralyzed, and He healed them.
